audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows contradicted the whys[] text beside them. The page gave Yone Levels 2 and 3 while whys[1] and whys[2] both say Irelia is ahead there, called Levels 4-5 and Level 6 skill windows while whys[3] and whys[4] say she wins them, and gave Yone first item while whys[5] calls it a skill window. The difficulty also read EVEN 6/10 on a 46.59% win rate over 3428 games.
audit.why: The packet chart — Irelia on Levels 1 through 6, Skill at first item, Yone at two items — matches the prose on all seven rows and matches a sub-50 win rate. The audited mirror agrees on five of them.
audit.corrected: Irelia, Irelia, Irelia, Irelia, Irelia, Skill, Yone; difficulty TRICKY at 7.5/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere despite the page being built around tracking one ability.
audit.why: Flawless Duet is 16s at rank 1 down to 10s — that is the only real gap in her kit. Bladesurge is 10s to 6s and refreshes outright on a Marked target or a kill, so near a wave it is effectively free. Defiant Dance is 20s to 12s. Vanguard's Edge is 125/105/85s. Your Soul Unbound falls 22s to 10s; Fate Sealed is 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Your window is the 16-second Flawless Duet gap with no minions left for her to reset off; her spikes are passive stacks and every wave that gives Bladesurge fuel.

audit.whatIsWrong: Defiant Dance (W) is never mentioned on the page; Vanguard's Edge is described as walling off your escape; Fate Sealed is described as setting up team knockups.
audit.why: Defiant Dance reduces the PHYSICAL damage she takes while she charges it — your crits are physical, so her damage reduction lands squarely on your burst and the charge is the tell for when not to dump it. Vanguard's Edge marks enemies and then forms a wall that damages and slows those who walk through it; Riot's text describes walking through it, not being blocked by it, so calling it a hard wall on your escape overstates it. Bladesurge heals her and refreshes on Marked targets or kills, which is what makes anti-heal and denying reset targets the core of the lane. Fate Sealed blinks behind the last champion in a line and pulls — no airborne; your knockup is Mortal Steel at two Gathering Storm stacks.
audit.corrected: Do not dump crit damage into a charging Defiant Dance. Her ultimate marks and then slows through a wall rather than sealing you in. Fate Sealed pulls, it does not knock up.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Flawless Duet and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 7.5/10. It is decided by how well you dodge Flawless Duet's 16s stun and deny her resets.

edits.after: First item stays close but her tempo lingers; commit when Flawless Duet is down, and never dump crits into a charging Defiant Dance (W) — it cuts physical damage.

notes: Six chart rows flipped in matched pairs onto the packet, which agrees with this page's own whys[] on all seven rows; the difficulty label moved from EVEN 6/10 to TRICKY 7.5/10 to match a 46.59% win rate over 3428 games. Defiant Dance (W) was missing from the page entirely and is the ability that most directly blunts Yone — it reduces the physical damage she takes while charging, which is exactly your crit burst. Softened two overstatements about Vanguard's Edge: Riot's text describes a wall that damages and slows enemies WALKING THROUGH it, not one that blocks movement, so 'walls your E escape' was rewritten rather than kept. No grounding claim was written for Flawless Duet despite the kit's grounding flag — Riot's description says damaged, stunned and Marked only.
unverified: Whether Flawless Duet actually grounds — the kit's derived flag says so, Riot's description does not mention it, so no claim was written.
